messages:
maria: Heads up — running long-context generator tests (200k tokens) and saw steady memory growth in the KV cache. Not a single big allocation spike, but we eventually hit OOM after ~45 minutes. Seems like fragmentation + reuse failure.

ben: Which allocator are we talking about (slab vs heaplet)? Any allocator metrics?

maria: It's the KV slab allocator. Quick dump from the test run: 
```
total_memory: 24GB
allocated: 18.9GB
free_small_chunks: 12,143
free_large_chunks: 37
largest_free: 48KB
avg_alloc_size: 47.6KB
free_frag_ratio: 0.42
compaction_runs: 2
compaction_time_ms: 420
```
Seems like many small free chunks but no contiguous large block for new allocations.

sasha: That avg_alloc_size vs block_size mismatch smells like internal fragmentation. We use 64KB block granularity, so allocations ~48KB always round up, leaving 16KB slack per allocation. Over many small allocations that adds up. Also compaction currently only triggers on eviction threshold, not proactively.

devon: We had a similar issue in late 2025 when chains of tool calls left lots of short-lived keys. Ideas: 1) add small-block free lists (8K/16K/32K pools) to reduce rounding waste; 2) proactive compaction when free_frag_ratio > 0.3 AND total_free < threshold; 3) background relinking (opportunistic) during low-gpu-util windows.

ben: All fine, but compaction is a potential tail-latency hazard. Have you measured latency impact of compact-on-idle vs compact-on-evict?

maria: Quick A/B results on our staging gen workload: compact-on-evict (baseline) vs compact-on-idle: 
- median latency: unchanged
- p95: +6ms
- p99: +30ms during compaction windows
- OOMs: baseline 3/10 runs, idle-compact 0/10 runs
So there's a small p99 hit but we avoid OOMs. Link to raw numbers: https://internal.metrics/kv/2070008110

perf-bot: perf-bot: uploaded flamegraph for the compact run: https://perf.internal/runs/2070008110/flame.svg

sasha: Another complementary approach: adaptive block sizing per model or route. Short-seq chat models get smaller base blocks; encoder-style long-context runs get larger contiguous pools. We can pick heuristics from per-route seq_length histogram.

devon: Also consider a light-weight compaction that only merges adjacent free small chunks into medium chunks (cheap) and do heavy merges during long idle windows. That reduces expensive full compactions.

ben: @maria can you produce a minimal reproducer (script + config) so we can put this into CI / perf-bench? I'll open a PR for a feature-flagged compaction mode and add metrics: compaction_runs, compaction_pause_ms, largest_free_after_compact.

maria: Will do. Reproducer command (staging): `python tools/kv_repro.py --tokens 200000 --batch 4 --alloc-pattern chat-like` — it spawns 8 parallel streams and hits the reuse patterns. Logs attached in the run page.

rachel: cc @oncall — ops: any concerns for enabling compaction by default in dedicated clusters? We should gate it behind rollout and toggle.

sasha: Agreed. Plan: feature-flag -> 2% traffic for 24h -> 10% -> 50%. Add compaction duration and p99 latency monitors. If p99 delta > 50ms revert.

maria: Thanks — I'll draft a short RFC with data + proposed config knobs: small_pool_sizes, frag_threshold, idle_compact_window_ms. PR incoming and I'll attach the reproducer. :shipit:

ben: Nice. Also add an instrumentation point in the kernel selector so we can correlate compaction events with kernel selection changes (if any).

devon: One more: add a TTL heuristic to drop unreferenced KV segments older than N tokens for routes that don't need full history. That saves space without compaction.

maria: Good call. Including TTL + compaction together might be the least invasive way to reduce steady-state fragmentation. I'll bundle them in the RFC and mark the rollout plan.

rachel: 👍 I'll coordinate the rollout schedule with infra.

maria: Logging action items: 1) reproducible script (maria) 2) PR with feature flag + metrics (ben) 3) RFC with configs + rollout (maria) 4) perf graphs & monitors (sasha + perf-bot).
